skills.description: Analyze bounded live or recorded Modbus samples for communication errors, response timing, missing or duplicate samples, stale and flat values, range and rate changes, counter resets or wraps, discrete transitions, and byte-order stability. Use for troubleshooting read-only captures.
skills.short_description: Analyze bounded live or recorded Modbus data
skills.default_prompt: Use $analyze-modbus-capture to find communication and signal-quality problems in this capture.

skills.description: Route an unclear Modbus engineering goal to one focused workflow. Use when the request does not provide enough information to select a focused skill. Also use as the safety stop for requests that ask for Modbus writes, broadcasts, network discovery, or unbounded polling. Do not use as the primary skill when a safe request names a concrete input, conversion, check, analysis, or target output that matches another skill.
skills.short_description: Route Modbus questions to tested workflows
skills.default_prompt: Use $ask-modbus to route my Modbus question.

skills.description: Build Node-RED, Modpoll, ModScan, or any non-empty combination from one reviewed Modbus map and one compiled read plan. Use when a user wants several tool outputs, a portable device pack, or is unsure which target to choose.
skills.short_description: Build any selected combination of tool outputs
skills.default_prompt: Use $build-modbus-tool-pack to generate Node-RED, Modpoll, and ModScan outputs from one map.

skills.description: Create a bounded read-only probe for collecting raw Modbus words through Node-RED, Modpoll, or ModScan. Use for sample acquisition before byte-order or datatype review. Use a target generator when the request is only to render a named output from an existing canonical map and read plan.
skills.short_description: Prepare a safe read-only raw sample probe
skills.default_prompt: Use $capture-modbus-sample to create a read-only probe for these raw registers.

skills.description: Compare two Modbus register maps using composite point identity and report added, removed, moved, and field-level changes. Use for firmware revisions, device variants, vendor-document updates, or project map drift.
skills.short_description: Compare maps with composite register identity
skills.default_prompt: Use $compare-modbus-maps to find added, removed, and changed register points.

skills.description: Compile reviewed Modbus points into deterministic, bounded read blocks for function codes 01 through 04 with route, unit, area, gap, interval, and target limits. Use before generating Node-RED, Modpoll, ModScan, or combined tool packs.
skills.short_description: Group points into safe bounded Modbus reads
skills.default_prompt: Use $compile-modbus-read-plan to build a traceable read-only poll plan.

skills.description: Run the complete Modbus register-map workflow from parsing through normalization, linting, evidence review, and human confirmation. Use for raw, imported, or messy maps that need end-to-end cleanup. Use lint-modbus-map instead when an already normalized map only needs deterministic checks.
skills.short_description: Run the complete register-map review flow
skills.default_prompt: Use $diagnose-modbus-map to parse, normalize, lint, and review this map.

skills.description: Evaluate raw Modbus register words as explicit byte and word layouts, signed and unsigned integers, and IEEE floating-point values from one immutable sample. Use for ABCD, BADC, CDAB, DCBA, endian, word-swap, implausible-value, or unknown encoding questions.
skills.short_description: Evaluate byte and word layouts from one read
skills.default_prompt: Use $evaluate-modbus-byte-order to compare all valid interpretations of these raw words.

skills.description: Extract candidate Modbus register rows and page evidence from a PDF manual. Use for device manuals, register-table PDFs, page-range extraction, OCR review, or when the user needs traceable rows rather than an unsupported summary.
skills.short_description: Extract register tables from Modbus manuals
skills.default_prompt: Use $extract-modbus-map-from-pdf to extract the register tables in this manual.

skills.description: Generate deterministic read-only artifacts for Witte Modbus Poll or the open-source gavinying/modpoll tool. Use when the user specifically requests a Modpoll or Modbus Poll artifact, saved poll setup, CLI configuration CSV, or raw probe.
skills.short_description: Generate Modbus Poll or modpoll artifacts
skills.default_prompt: Use $generate-modpoll-config to create the correct Modpoll profile for this map.

skills.description: Generate deterministic, documented, read-only ModScan setup and poll-plan artifacts from a canonical map and read plan. Use when the user specifically requests a ModScan setup, probe, or reusable read plan.
skills.default_prompt: Use $generate-modscan-config to create a documented read-only ModScan plan.

skills.description: Generate deterministic, read-only Node-RED Modbus flow JSON from a canonical map and compiled read plan. Use when the user specifically requests a Node-RED import, reusable flow, or probe-mode flow. Use capture-modbus-sample first when sample acquisition is the goal and no probe request exists.
skills.short_description: Generate a safe deterministic Modbus flow
skills.default_prompt: Use $generate-node-red-flow to create a read-only Node-RED flow from this reviewed map.

skills.description: Define a safe declarative text or CSV export format from a documented example and render it deterministically from a canonical Modbus map. Use for simple custom tool formats that do not require graphs, opaque binaries, or several related collections.
skills.short_description: Create a safe declarative text exporter
skills.default_prompt: Use $infer-custom-modbus-export-format to define a safe reusable text export format.

skills.description: Validate a normalized Modbus map for duplicate identities, overlaps, invalid ranges, datatype-width conflicts, area and function-code conflicts, unresolved fields, unsafe writes, and scoped byte-order inconsistencies. Use when explicit map fields exist and the goal is deterministic validation only. Use diagnose-modbus-map for end-to-end cleanup of a raw or messy map.
skills.short_description: Find unsafe or inconsistent map entries
skills.default_prompt: Use $lint-modbus-map to check this register map for conflicts and unsafe assumptions.

skills.description: Normalize a candidate Modbus map into explicit protocol offsets, register areas, unit identifiers, datatypes, word counts, access values, and byte-order states. Use after parsing or to represent mixed or unresolved source conventions without a requested map-wide conversion. Use remap-modbus-addresses when the user asks to convert a map between known conventions.
skills.default_prompt: Use $normalize-modbus-map to normalize this map without guessing unresolved fields.

skills.description: Parse Modbus register maps from CSV, JSON, XML, XLSX, or structured text into candidate-map artifacts with source values, rejected rows, warnings, assumptions, and holds. Use when a user supplies a register list or wants a machine-readable map without silent engineering guesses.
skills.short_description: Parse register maps with evidence and holds
skills.default_prompt: Use $parse-modbus-map to parse this register map into a reviewed artifact.

skills.description: Preview and apply a requested map-wide conversion between protocol offsets, one-based offsets, and Modicon reference notation, with explicit areas and collision checks. Use when the source and target conventions are known. Use normalize-modbus-map first when source conventions or engineering fields remain mixed or unresolved.
skills.short_description: Convert address conventions with collision checks
skills.default_prompt: Use $remap-modbus-addresses to preview a safe address-convention conversion.

skills.description: Review Modbus parsing evidence, rejected rows, inferred values, assumptions, warnings, and blocking holds. Use before promoting a candidate map, after PDF extraction, or when a user needs to know which register-map fields are confirmed versus inferred.
skills.short_description: Review source evidence, assumptions, and holds
skills.default_prompt: Use $review-modbus-evidence to show what is confirmed and what still needs review.
